title: Tailored Education for Aging and Cognitive Health: A Health Behavior Change Intervention for Midlife Adults at Risk for Alzheimer's Disease and Related Dementias
official: Testing the Efficacy of a Personalized Multi-Domain Behavioral Intervention for Alzheimer's Disease and Related Dementias Risk Reduction in Midlife
summary: This Stage II behavioral intervention development project will examine the efficacy of a multi-domain health behavior intervention for primary prevention of Alzheimer's disease and related dementias (ADRD) in middle age.
conditions: Alzheimer's Disease and Alzheimer's Disease Related Dementias (AD/ADRD)
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

1. Age 40-69 years
2. Normal cognition (Telephone Interview for Cognitive Status-Modified \> 32)
3. English language fluency
4. Participants must have at least two of six dementia risk factors:

   1. BMI in the overweight or obesity range ( \>24.9)
   2. Systolic blood pressure in the "elevated" range or higher (\>120 mmHg)
   3. LDL cholesterol outside the "optimal" range (\>100 mg/dL)
   4. HbA1C in the prediabetes or diabetes range (\> 5.6%)
   5. APOE e4 allele
   6. First-degree relative with ADRD
5. Participants must have suboptimal engagement in at least one core health behavior:

   1. Diet: Mediterranean Diet Adherence Screener (MEDAS) total score \< 10
   2. Physical activity: \<120 minutes of moderate-intensity or \<60 minutes of vigorous-intensity physical activity per week
   3. Sleep: \<=7 hours of sleep per night (past-week average)

Exclusion Criteria:

1. History of serious mental illness (i.e., schizophrenia, bipolar disorder)
2. Current Beck Depression Inventory score \> 28
3. Prior diagnosis of Mild or Major Neurocognitive Disorder
4. History of neurodevelopmental disorder (e.g., intellectual disability)
5. Severe physical disability or unstable medical conditions that prevent safe engagement in recommended study activities (e.g., physical activity)
6. Current alcohol or substance use disorder based on self-report
7. Current enrollment in an ADRD prevention clinical trial.
